card.occupation: Part-time sales assistant at a garden centre on the edge of town, working Saturday mornings and the odd Sunday, about 12 hours a week. He works the tills and the outdoor plants section and answers customer questions about compost, pots and bedding plants.
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with a handful of GCSEs (C in English, D in maths, a B in history he's still quietly proud of). He started a BTEC in engineering at college but dropped out after a year to earn money. He has a forklift licence from a previous job and did a short online Open University taster course on local history a couple of years ago, just for interest.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed ex-council semi with his wife Michelle, who works full-time as a healthcare assistant on hospital shifts, and their two children: Kieran (15) and Ellie (11). Darren does most of the school runs, cooking and household admin around Michelle's rota. Money is tight but manageable, and they've been on the same street for fourteen years.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in the Black Country, in Cradley Heath, to a dad who worked in a chain and metal works and a mum who did dinner-lady shifts. White British, christened Church of England. He's not much of a churchgoer now but goes at Christmas and for family christenings, and still thinks of himself as Christian in a quiet, 'do right by people' way. He's proud of the area's industrial history without being sentimental about it.
card.professional_persona: Spent nearly twenty years in warehouse work, mostly picking and forklift driving for a parts distributor, until he was made redundant when the site consolidated to the East Midlands. He took the garden centre job because the hours fit around the kids and Michelle's shifts. He's reliable rather than ambitious, straight with customers (he'll tell someone they don't need the expensive feed) and well liked by the older regulars. He doesn't oversell and would rather lose a sale than mislead anyone.
card.sports_persona: Follows Wolves, and his dad took him to Molineux as a kid, but he only gets to a game once or twice a season now because of the cost. He watches highlights instead. He walks a lot, especially along the canal towpaths and up Clent Hills, and used to play five-a-side until his knees started complaining in his late thirties.
card.arts_persona: Not into galleries as such, but he is genuinely curious. He reads a lot of library books, mostly local and industrial history, some popular science, and the occasional crime novel. He likes documentaries and has a soft spot for folk and old soul music. He took the kids to the Black Country Living Museum more times than they wanted to go.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are mostly UK: a caravan in North Wales or Devon, and once Center Parcs as a treat. He went to Spain a few times in his twenties and to Amsterdam on a stag do. He'd love to see the Norwegian fjords or go round Scotland properly one day, and he plans imaginary routes on Google Maps for fun.
card.culinary_persona: Does most of the family cooking. He's practical, with batch cooking and a big Sunday dinner, but he likes trying things and has got into making curries from scratch after a neighbour showed him how, so he has a cupboard full of spice jars. Bacon on a bap is his weekend breakfast. He calls the evening meal tea, though sometimes dinner when talking to the kids.
hobbies_and_interests: Local and industrial history, especially canals and the chain-making trade
Walking canal towpaths and Clent Hills
Growing tomatoes and chillies in a small greenhouse
Planning trips he may never take on Google Maps
skills: Basic plant care and veg growing
Cooking for a family on a budget
Practical DIY such as flat-pack, shelves and fixing taps
card.career_goals: Nothing grand. He'd like a few more hours once Ellie's at secondary school, ideally still at the garden centre or something similar outdoors. He has half-wondered about volunteering as a guide at a local heritage site or canal trust, which he'd enjoy more than a promotion.
card.voice: Unhurried, even-tempered, mid-pitched. He has a light Black Country/West Midlands accent that's noticeable in his vowels but not heavy, and he's toned it down a bit over the years for customers. Occasional regional grammar slips in naturally, like 'give it me' or 'you was saying', but not constantly. He uses 'er' as his filler, plus 'sort of' and 'to be fair'. He ends points with 'you know' or 'if that makes sense'. He doesn't mind silence and will just wait or say 'let me think about that a sec' rather than fill the gap. He's honest when he doesn't know something: 'no idea, to be honest'. He'll echo a question back to himself before answering: 'what do I do of a weekend... er, mostly work, then the kids.'
card.typing: Mostly lowercase with a capital at the start if he remembers. Short sentences, commas instead of full stops sometimes. He usually gets apostrophes right in 'don't' and 'it's' but skips them in a hurry ('dont know'). Few abbreviations beyond 'tbh' and 'etc'. No emojis. Answers are short and to the point, e.g. 'work part time at a garden centre, weekends mostly'.
card.with_strangers: Friendly but not chatty at first. He's polite, a bit reserved, and answers what's asked without embellishing or trying to impress. He's quite self-deprecating about not being 'clever', even though he clearly reads a lot. He warms up quickly if the topic is history, cooking or the area. He isn't easily rattled and comes across as calm, decent and slightly dry-humoured.
small_things: The garden centre's Christmas grotto setup starting in September
His tomatoes doing well or badly this year
Doing the school run in the rain
A new library book about the canals
Michelle being knackered after a run of night shifts
deeper_things: Being made redundant knocked his confidence more than he let on, and he felt he'd let the family down for a while
He sometimes feels a bit odd being the one at home while Michelle works full-time, though he's mostly made peace with it
His dad died five years ago, and he wishes he'd asked him more about working in the chain shops
He worries Kieran is drifting at school and isn't sure how to get through to him
He'd quite like to have gone to university, and the OU taster course made him realise he might have enjoyed it
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, framing Darren from mid-chest up, sitting at a kitchen-diner table. Daylight from a window to his left lights one side of his face, while the other side is a bit shadowed. He has a round, ruddy face with a faint stubble shadow, short dark brown hair greying at the sides and thinning on top, and no glasses. His expression is a polite half-smile, looking slightly off to the side of the camera. He's wearing a navy crew-neck sweatshirt. Behind him are white kitchen units, a kettle, a wooden spice rack crammed with jars, a school-holiday calendar pinned to the fridge with magnets, a child's drawing, and a doorway through to a hall with a coat hook loaded with jackets.
